findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (Senate roll call)
findings.note: The Senator's vote list shows Aye on Second Reading of HB 958, Election Law Changes, on 7/28/2026 at 6:13 PM, tally 28 to 13 (9 not voting, per the list), result PASS. The bill text (Fifth Edition, fetched from ncleg.gov) includes: a longer deadline (third to fifth business day after the election) for a voter without photo ID to bring ID to the county board for a provisional ballot to count (Sec. 1.2(c)); the same longer deadline for voters whose ID numbers did not match at registration (Sec. 1.2(b)); a temporary rule treating certain Class C drivers licenses with extended expiration dates as valid photo ID for voting through 2027 (Sec. 2.9); and handling of voter registration applications that indicate lack of citizenship (Sec. 2.10). The bill page says it was passed on Third Reading in the Senate on 7/28/2026 and the House concurred 8/4/2026; I did not find a separate Third Reading line in the Senator's vote list.

findings.passage: “President Joe Biden has been asleep at the wheel the past four years, letting millions of people illegally cross the border into our country. Now, as voters are fleeing the Democratic party in droves, Democrats are seeking to fill the gap by extending voting rights to noncitizens,” Sens. Brad Overcash (R-Gaston), Buck Newton (R-Wilson), and Warren Daniel (R-Burke) said. “To combat this movement, we are empowering North Carolinians to approve a constitutional amendment to make it crystal clear that our elections are for U.S. citizens only.”
findings.note: Joint Senate press release statement from three senators including Overcash, on the Senate passing the citizens-only voting amendment (HB 1074). The same release covers a separate amendment to require photo ID for mail and provisional ballots, quoted from a different senator, not Overcash.

findings.passage: We've got an opportunity to empower the people of North Carolina to amend their own constitution and declare that citizens and only citizens of the state of North Carolina are allowed to vote in our elections,
findings.note: Direct quote of Overcash in a news story (Yahoo News, reprint) about the citizens-only voting amendment on the November 2024 ballot. Article text on the page is straight quote marks around the sentence; closing comma is part of the quote as printed.
